answer: Propose no signup grants: a listing-day costs an ID-bound receipt for sending 1 GiB of assigned encrypted karst-map shards to a remote metering mirror. Validators check mirror signatures and spend receipts once; bad or missing proof means no listing. A colluding mirror can certify a fable instead of traffic. Hardware is reusable; traffic and power recur; no stake. Pooling can cut unit prices, not bytes; this meters service, not owners. Ten listings require 10 GiB/day under one ID or ten, even with shared servers or parallel sends.
